statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 19%, at the top of the low band, while Stress at 55% remains the elevated component.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is EA_ON on Tail 19%. The elevated component is Stress at 55%, carried by a ten-year at its highest since 2007, roughly 73% odds on an October Fed hike and a four-month low in consumer sentiment, rather than by observed Nasdaq-100 trend persistence. The narrow danger window runs from 19:00Z to the 21:00Z CME weekly futures halt, covering the Friday power hour and pre-weekend position squaring. Beyond 21:00Z the remaining twenty-one published slots are halted time in which no mean-reversion failure can develop.
headline: Session low beneath Thursday's close fully recovered and the marginal high not held, with VIX under 15 and semis leading; two-way tape keeps Tail in the low band
body: The Nasdaq-100 trades 30,642.37, up 0.54% against a 30,478.86 previous close, inside a 30,413.59 to 30,667.56 session range that has not been extended in either direction for several hours. The structural point is that both directions have been paid: the session low broke beneath Thursday's close and was bought back in full, roughly 229 points, while the marginal high has not been held, with price some 25 points below it. That is retracement working symmetrically rather than the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension signature that would justify a higher Tail. Volatility is decaying alongside it, with VIX 14.98, down 4.40%, close to its 14.86 session low and well beneath the 15.94 high. Cross-assets describe relief inside a stressed regime. The ten-year is 5.20%, up 4 basis points and off its 5.23% intraday high, after a three-session selloff that carried it to its highest since 2007. The five-year is 5.03%. WTI is $92.29, down 2.45%, with Brent near $99, on reports of US-Iran negotiators exploring a phased agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Semiconductors lead, with SOX +1.69% at 12,703.13 and a 12,549.59 session low that held above Thursday's close, while the megacap complex is split, so the leadership is sector-wide rather than concentrated in one name. Friday's data cut both ways. August durable goods printed 0.0% against a -0.4% consensus with core capital-goods orders +1.6%, while the final September Michigan sentiment fell to 48.1, a four-month low, and one-year inflation expectations rose to 4.6% from 4.0%. Futures price roughly 73% odds of a hike at the October 27-28 FOMC. That combination is a genuinely difficult environment and is what the elevated Stress reading measures. It is not, on current evidence, a pathological price path, so Tail stays inside the low band. Shared Finviz context was collected at 14:12Z with partial coverage and no futures section, which places it outside the 90-minute freshness window; it was therefore not used as supporting evidence and this assessment rests on independently fetched live quotes and primary reporting. The dominant feature of the forward horizon is mechanical: the CME weekly index-futures halt at 21:00Z, after which twenty-one of the twenty-four published slots are untradeable time.

lookbackSummary: The trailing 24 hours stayed inside a narrow band: Tail between 17% and 22%, Stress between 54% and 59%, and Confidence between 86% and 88%, alternating between EA_ON and WATCH without approaching the block threshold at any point. Dominant mode ran mixed through the US evening, normal across the 01:00Z to 05:00Z Asian hours, then produced trend-up readings during the European morning and the US pre-market before reverting to mixed for the cash session. The 13:00Z slot has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable with null assessment fields. The last three published hours read 19%, 18% and 19% Tail, which is the level the current assessment continues.
outlookSummary: The near-term path keeps Tail inside the low and watch bands, rising to 21% across the Friday power hour and the 20:00Z cash close, which together define the narrow danger window from 19:00Z to 21:00Z. The defining feature of this horizon is the CME weekly index-futures halt at 21:00Z: the last twenty-one hourly slots are halted, untradeable time in which no mean-reversion failure can develop, so Tail falls to a 10% then 9% residual covering weekend gap risk and the published action returns to EA_ON throughout. Stress eases only to 53% because the rates, policy and sentiment backdrop is carried forward rather than resolved, and Confidence decays steadily from 86% to 54% to label an assessment that cannot be refreshed while every relevant venue is closed. The Sunday 22:00Z reopen, and with it the gap risk from the unresolved Hormuz negotiation, falls outside this window.

Tail is lifted to 21% conditionally for late position-squaring into a weekend that carries an unresolved Hormuz negotiation. That is a checkpoint, not observed structure: the invalidation would be a break of 30,667.56 or 30,413.59 that then refuses to retrace.

forecast.analysis: US cash trading has closed by this slot and only the final hour of CME index futures remains before the weekly halt. Liquidity thins sharply, which can widen ranges but also caps how long any one-way path could run. Tail eases to 17% on that shortened runway rather than on any observed change in structure.
drivers: US cash session closed; only thin post-close futures remain
One hour left before the 21:00Z CME weekly futures halt
Thin liquidity can widen ranges without sustaining a trend

forecast.analysis: The CME weekly index-futures halt begins at 21:00Z and runs to the Sunday reopen, so this slot is untradeable time for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. No mean-reversion failure can develop while every relevant venue is closed. Tail drops to a 10% residual that carries weekend headline and gap risk only.
drivers: CME weekly index-futures halt begins at 21:00Z
No tradeable NQ or NAS100 price path during the halt
Residual Tail reflects weekend headline and gap risk only

forecast.analysis: First full hour of the weekend halt. There is no venue in which a price path can form, so the published scores describe carried-forward regime risk rather than anything observable. The unresolved US-Iran talks on a phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz remain the most plausible source of a weekend repricing headline.
drivers: Weekend halt in force; no observable NQ or NAS100 price path
Unresolved US-Iran phased Hormuz negotiation as headline risk
WTI $92.29 (-2.45%) already reflects part of that relief

forecast.analysis: Late Friday US evening. Wire services publish week-in-review and positioning copy in this window, which occasionally moves weekend sentiment but cannot move a halted contract. Tail settles to its 9% weekend residual and Confidence continues to decay because the assessment cannot be refreshed against live prices.

Week-in-review and positioning copy typically lands in this hour
Confidence decays because no live price refresh is possible

Two-way Friday tape can be neither confirmed nor invalidated

It remains a Stress and Confidence input; no NQ path exists in this slot to make it a Tail input.

A hawkish run of remarks would most plausibly show up first in the rates market, which is the Stress channel, before it could become an index price-path question.
